kind: pre-dispatch assessment only: environment feasibility + defect reproduction; no product/test code changed, PBK-30 criteria NOT executed
model_observed: reported to the coordinator in the session handoff, not recorded in Git
environment: Cloud container Ubuntu 24.04, Docker 29.6.2 (dockerd started in-container), Supabase CLI 2.33.9 via npx, images from Docker Hub (SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=docker.io; public.ecr.aws pulls return 403 here): postgres 15.8.1.085, gotrue v2.177.0, storage-api v1.26.0, realtime v2.41.11 (locally patched, see recipe). Excluded: studio, imgproxy, vector, logflare, edge-runtime, supavisor. Next.js `npm run dev` with gitignored .env.development.local pointing at 127.0.0.1:54321. Synthetic dev user only; remote project untouched (paused).
environment_recipe: Kernel has no IPv6: realtime v2.41.11 hardcodes an :inet6 HTTP listener (runtime.exs line 151) and exits with eafnosupport; rebuilt the image locally with that line set to [:inet]. Container-only workaround, not for the repo.

Clean `supabase start` cannot apply repo migrations (see finding F1). Workaround used: start with migrations moved aside, then apply each migration with psql as `postgres`, re-running only the 3 failing files as `supabase_admin`.
Dev mode needs auth user id 37770da5-4fdb-4b75-9dc2-3bf9b2f90ed8 (see F2); created via local admin API with email dev@properbooky.com and the app's default dev password.

findings.summary: Migrations 20240324000000_add_storage_bucket.sql (CREATE INDEX on storage.objects), 20240325000000_enhance_storage_security.sql (CREATE INDEX + CREATE TRIGGER on storage.objects) and 20240329000000_setup_default_books.sql (CREATE INDEX on storage.objects) fail as `postgres` with 'must be owner of table objects' on current local images. `supabase start` aborts at 20240324. The other 11 migrations apply as `postgres`.
findings.evidence: psql per-file apply log (scratch migrate.log); supabase-start5.log

findings.severity: high (dev mode unusable on a fresh stack)
findings.summary: lib/hooks/use-auth.ts dev bootstrap signs in or signs up dev@properbooky.com, but sign-up creates a random user id while the client uses hardcoded FLAGS.DEV_USER_ID. Every default-book insert is rejected by RLS (42501, HTTP 403 x30 on POST /rest/v1/books) and the library stays empty. Works only if the auth user already has that fixed id.
findings.evidence: probe1 run before fixture: 30x 'new row violates row-level security policy for table books'

findings.summary: Default-book provisioning races. Several mounted hook instances each check-then-insert, so a fresh dev user received 8 identical 'Sample PDF Book' rows.
findings.evidence: SELECT on books after first successful load: 8 rows, same title/user

findings.summary: Dashboard `/` widgets ActivityFeed and ReadingStats query public.reading_activities and public.reading_statistics. Both are dropped by 20240321000000_fix_stats_cleanup.sql, so PostgREST returns 404 42P01. The UI shows empty cards or 'No reading statistics available' and the console shows a 404.
lib/utils/default-books.ts queries books before the dev session exists, so the anon role gets 401 'permission denied for table books' with a console error on every load.
findings.evidence: probe2: HTTP 401 GET books?select=id... before the authenticated 200

suspected_not_yet_reproduced: Reset page (app/auth/reset-password/page.tsx) calls updateUser with no explicit code exchange or session check. Needs a run against `next build && next start` with Inbucket email capture; dev mode forces the auth bypass.
Metadata sliders persist on every onValueChange tick, and `|| 0.5` / `|| 2.5` render a stored 0 as the default.
updateBook: a key passed as undefined overwrites the stored value and is then dropped by the JSON round-trip.
